study_design: retrospective TMA-based immunohistochemical study (single TMA block selected from a larger cohort); chi-square tests on dichotomised CD8/FOXP3 ratio
conflicts_of_interest: No potential conflicts of interest declared
population_description: Invasive penile SCC; 1 TMA block, 144 spots from 35 patients (parent cohort 108 patients, 528 spots); 79 spots from 23 patients evaluable. Spots by subtype: usual 38, warty-basaloid 30, basaloid 8, warty 3. Grade 1/2/3: 7/29/43 spots.
primary_aim_as_stated: Characterise the CD8+/FOXP3+ ratio in penile SCC: (1) quantify infiltrates in intratumoral and stromal compartments; (2) describe the ratio distribution; (3) explore associations with histologic subtype and grade (Introduction, p. 2).
key_finding_time: Intratumoral median CD8 5 (IQR 0-15) and FOXP3 4 (1-12.5) per HPF; stromal CD8 22 (7.5-49) and FOXP3 38 (15-71.5) per HPF. CD8>FOXP3 in 40.5% of spots (tumour) and 23% (stroma); CD8<=FOXP3 predominates in both (p. 3).
key_finding_hpv: HPV by morphology only (WHO subtype). Stromal ratio CD8<=FOXP3 in 87% (33/38) of HPV-independent vs 68% (28/41) of HPV-associated spots, P=.09 (not significant). Tumour ratio vs HPV category P=.682 (p. 3).
limitations_as_stated: Retrospective; N=23 patients; TMA sampling; selection bias from a single TMA block; no clinical follow-up; HPV inferred morphologically; no functional immune assessment (p. 5).
other_key_outcomes: Ratio vs grade: tumour P=.529, stroma P=.660. Ratio vs original subtype: tumour P=.333, stroma P=.114. No correction for multiple comparisons (declared exploratory). Ratio dichotomised at <=1 vs >1 (pp. 3-4).

population_description: Narrative overview of penile neoplasms, mainly penile SCC; no primary cohort.
primary_aim_as_stated: Overview of current knowledge on the molecular pathology of penile neoplasms: molecular classification, key biomarkers relevant to disease management, and emerging therapeutic strategies based on molecular profiling (Introduction, p. 14).
key_finding_time: TILs, particularly CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes, associated with better outcomes; HPV+ tumours 'frequently' show a more robust immune response than HPV- (one cited study). PD-L1 expressed in 40-62% of penile SCC, higher in HPV-negative tumours (pp. 16-17).
key_finding_hpv: HPV-associated SCC: p16 overexpressed, p53 wild-type/low. HPV-independent SCC: p16 negative, p53 often mutated/overexpressed. 2022 WHO classification stratifies by HPV status (pp. 15, 17; Table 1 p. 18; Fig. 1 p. 19).
key_finding_prognosis: HPV prognostic value described as complex (some studies show no association with overall survival); p16 linked to better outcomes in some cohorts; p53 overexpression and PD-L1 positivity linked to worse outcomes; elevated NLR and CRP linked to worse outcomes (pp. 19-20).
key_finding_immunotherapy: Checkpoint inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab, ipilimumab) described as promising in advanced disease, 'especially in HPV-positive tumors'; no trial data presented (pp. 17, 20).
limitations_as_stated: NR - no limitations section; authors only call for larger trials and better predictive biomarkers (pp. 20-21).
other_key_outcomes: WHO 2022 HPV-associated vs HPV-independent subtypes; PeIN types; TP53/CDKN2A/TERT/PIK3CA alterations; HPV implicated in 50-70% of SCC (literature figure, p. 17); practice points: test all penile SCC for HPV with p16 IHC plus PCR in equivocal cases (p. 21).
extraction_note: Independent extraction by P.B. (2026-10-26/27), blinded to the earlier single-reviewer record, replaces the previous row (A.C. is a co-author). Source is a narrative review: no Methods section, no search strategy; MMAT = NA. hpv_stratified=yes reflects review organisation by HPV status, not an analytic stratification (decision taken by REV-PAOLA). Internal inconsistencies in source: (1) PD-L1 higher in HPV-negative per text p. 17 vs 'often expressed' in HPV-associated per Table 1 p. 18; (2) immunotherapy 'especially in HPV-positive' (p. 20) vs higher PD-L1 in HPV-negative (p. 17); (3) HPV-16/18 linked to poorer prognosis (p. 17) vs HPV+ possibly better prognosis (p. 19). study_design: retrospective TMA-based immunohistochemical study with linear-regression 'machine learning' model (explained variance, 80/20 train/test split)
conflicts_of_interest: The authors declare no conflict of interests.
population_description: Invasive penile SCC, 108 patients from consultation files of one author; cases selected by FFPE block availability; 1-4 blocks per case; 4 TMAs, 528 spots. Subtypes: usual 45, warty-basaloid 24, warty 16, basaloid 11, papillary 9, verrucous 2, sarcomatoid 1.
primary_aim_as_stated: Discern the relationship between pathologic features (histologic subtype, grade, host response) and PD-L1 and CD8 expression (Introduction, p. 3).
key_finding_time: PD-L1 in tumour cells positive (>0%) in 63% of 504 evaluable spots, median 5%; PD-L1 in intratumoral lymphocytes median 5 (n=497). CD8 median 4 intratumoral (n=506) and 19 peritumoral (n=503). Tumour vs lymphocyte correlations: PD-L1 rho=0.47, CD8 rho=0.37. By subtype: higher tumour PD-L1 in sarcomatoid (100%), basaloid (25%), warty-basaloid (20%), P<0.0001. By grade: tumour PD-L1 0/1/15% in G1/G2/G3 (P<0.0001); intratumoral CD8 1/2/6 (P<0.00001); peritumoral CD8 no association (P=0.92). Host response associated with higher PD-L1 and CD8 in all compartments (P<0.0001) (pp. 7-10).
key_finding_prognosis: NR - no outcome data analysed; authors suggest prognostic/predictive potential (abstract, p. 14).
limitations_as_stated: TMA may not capture intratumoral heterogeneity (whole-section analysis suggested); HPV status not assessed; relation to genetic alterations unexplored (p. 13).
other_key_outcomes: Explained variance, tumour PD-L1: subtype 13.5%, host response 6.5%, grade 3.5%, subtype+host response 20%. CD8 intratumoral: host response 15.0%. CD8 peritumoral: host response 21.1%. No cross-validation reported (pp. 5-11).
